mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.2% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as monetary policy accommodates economic growth without inflationary pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.2% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in FEDFUNDS above 0.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuation multiples, which produces negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and real financial services spending (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% monthly indicate robust consumer demand, accelerating corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 0.5% in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Labor market slack (UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.2% monthly) reflects weak consumer spending and profit growth, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to recessionary expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.2% per month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.2% per month (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) growth above 0.5% monthly signals accelerating consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns through immediate corporate revenue momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST grows > 0.5% monthly (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) indicates economic contraction, reducing corporate output and earnings growth, which causes negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rises in CPIAUCSL (>0.3% monthly) and FEDFUNDS (>0.1% monthly) signal successful inflation control without recession, boosting investor confidence and generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% annually), sustained economic momentum drives positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns through continued corporate earnings acceleration.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% annually (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
